claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a priest (presbyter) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was active in the first half of the fifth century and died around 450.
Hesychius became presbyter at Jerusalem in 412 according to Theophanes Confessor.
The homily was delivered on August 15, shortly after the Council of Ephesus (431), which had proclaimed Mary as Mother of God (Theotokos).
The homily was written for a feast of the Virgin Mary celebrating her as Mother of God, when August 15 was dedicated to the veneration of Mary as Mother of God.
The feast of the Dormition or Assumption of Mary was only definitively fixed to August 15 later, under Emperor Maurice (582-602).
The homily was published by Ducaeus in the Bibliotheca Patrum Gr. Lat. vol. ii. p. 417, with a Latin version by Joannes Picus of Paris in the Bibl. Patrum (vol. xii. p. 185, &c.).
Hesychius is credited with the earliest known liturgical addresses on the Virgin Mary.
The works of Hesychius have been transmitted in part as manuscripts, with some works confused with those of other authors named Hesychius in Migne's edition.
A comprehensive critical edition of the homilies transmitted under Hesychius' name was published by Michel Aubineau.
